input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 gives us (Customer) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days before the effective termination date — matching the preferred 30-day position. Termination carries no penalty or early-termination fee: we owe only accrued Fees and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10.2). Section 7.1 also bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges, and no early-termination fee appears anywhere in the document. Conversely, Vendor's termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and the narrow IP-remedy carve-out in Section 20 (which expressly bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services); Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (8.1) and none at renewal. Section 8.2 non-renewal is also Customer-controlled. Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-default term, not a termination penalty, so it falls outside this rule.
